routes.label: Find each average speed and compare

question: Cars \(A\) and \(B\) travel the same distance. Car \(A\) travels half that distance at \(u\) miles per hour and half at \(v\) miles per hour. Car \(B\) travels half the time at \(u\) miles per hour and half at \(v\) miles per hour. The average speed of Car \(A\) is \(x\) miles per hour and that of Car \(B\) is \(y\) miles per hour. Then we always have
solution:
Average speed is total distance divided by total time. The travel speeds \(u\) and \(v\) are understood to be positive, so all travel times and denominators below are positive.

Let the common distance be \(L>0\). Car \(A\) spends \(L/(2u)\) hours on its first half and \(L/(2v)\) hours on its second half. Its average speed is therefore
\[
x=\frac{L}{L/(2u)+L/(2v)}
=\frac{2uv}{u+v}.
\]
For Car \(B\), let the total travel time be \(T>0\). It covers distances \(uT/2\) and \(vT/2\), so
\[
y=\frac{uT/2+vT/2}{T}
=\frac{u+v}{2}.
\]
To compare these expressions, subtract them and look for a nonnegative square:
\[
\begin{aligned}
y-x
&=\frac{(u+v)^2-4uv}{2(u+v)}\\
&=\frac{(u-v)^2}{2(u+v)}\ge0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The numerator is nonnegative and the denominator is positive. Equality occurs when \(u=v\); otherwise \(x<y\). Thus the relation that always holds is \(\boxed{x\le y}\), choice A.
